title: Leaderboard Hacking: Preference-Based Model Evaluations are Vulnerable to Manipulation
abstract: arXiv:2611.14769v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Arena-style rankings of language models are a widely used evaluation framework in online leaderboards, research papers, and model evaluation in production. These rankings aim to realistically assess model performance using pairwise comparisons of anonymous models on user prompts, aggregating votes via the Bradley-Terry model to produce the final ranking. However, we find that these leaderboards are highly vulnerable to several manipulation strategies that unscrupulous providers could use to boost a model's rank: strategic voting (individual votes that boost a model's rank, including votes on irrelevant models), strategic prompting (choosing prompts that favor a model), and strategic nomination (boosting the rank of a model by inserting irrelevant models). translated_title: 排行榜作弊：基于偏好的模型评估易受操纵
translated_abstract: 竞技场式的语言模型排名是在线排行榜、研究论文以及生产环境模型评估中广泛使用的评估框架。这些排名旨在通过对匿名模型在用户提示词上的成对比较来真实评估模型性能，并通过Bradley-Terry模型聚合投票以生成最终排名。然而，我们发现这些排行榜极易受到多种操纵策略的影响，不良提供商可能利用这些策略来提升模型的排名：策略性投票（提升模型排名的个人投票，包括对无关模型的投票）、策略性提示（选择有利于某模型的提示词）以及策略性提名（通过插入无关模型来提升某模型的排名）。我们在公开排行榜数据上展示了这些操纵效果，分析了导致这些漏洞的成因，并描述了针对每种攻击的防御方法。
tldr: 该论文揭示Arena式语言模型排行榜极易受到策略性投票、策略性提示和策略性提名等操纵手段的攻击，并通过公开数据验证了这些漏洞，同时提出了相应的防御措施。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that Arena-style language model leaderboards are highly vulnerable to manipulation through strategic voting, strategic prompting, and strategic nomination, demonstrates these vulnerabilities on public leaderboard data, and proposes safeguards against each attack.
